title: Scalar boundary-reflection convergence
question: Does scalar contamination generated by the one-dimensional homogeneous incoming boundary converge away relative to an equal-spacing causally disconnected extended-domain control?
prediction: Normalized reflection energy falls by more than a factor of ten at each refinement, reaches below 1e-5 on 128 cells, the reflected amplitude stays below 2e-9, scalar constraints remain bounded, and the extended far boundary is causally disconnected.
falsifier: Nonconvergent reflection, excessive fine contamination, scalar-constraint growth, or causal contact with the extended far boundary falsifies the qualification.
controls: Every finite grid is paired with a twice-long equal-spacing control sharing its lower boundary and initial pulse.
The extended upper boundary at x=1.5 lies beyond the duration-0.6 light cone of the pulse centered at x=0.2.
The comparison region x<0.4 excludes the outgoing control pulse after boundary encounter.
The effective mass uses the canonical discovery scalar mass and carrier coupling at homogeneous carrier density 0.03.
seed_rationale: The Gaussian pulse and RK4 trajectories are deterministic.
